paper.title_en: Learning to find cosmic filaments with graph neural networks
paper.abstract_en: Inferring the large-scale structure of the Universe from galaxy surveys is a fundamental challenge in cosmology. In particular, cosmic filaments form an extended and geometrically complex network whose underlying structure cannot be reconstructed from discrete galaxy catalogs without uncertainty. We investigate a generative approach to filament finding based on flow matching and graph neural networks. The learned model reproduces key statistical properties of the target filament distribution while generating a distribution over possible filament configurations, demonstrating its ability to model uncertainty. Our work provides a first step towards probabilistic inference of the cosmic web directly from galaxy surveys. More broadly, these results demonstrate the potential of conditional generative models for reconstructing filament-like structures from sparse observational tracers.
